item.title: Jalen Williams has leg surgery; will be re-evaluated before 2027 NBA playoffs
item.description: The first step in a grueling process, the Oklahoma City Thunder have announced on Wednesday that Jalen Williams has finally had surgery to repair his fractured fibula and dislocated ankle. He will be re-evaluated before the end of the 2026-27 regular season. The surgery was performed by Dr. Martin O’Malley at the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York City, with Thunder medical personnel present. Williams sustained the two injuries in OKC's win over the LA Clippers this past Sunday. With a little over a minute to go, he went up for a driving layup. Kris Dunn collided with him mid-air. He landed nastily on his left leg as it snapped backward. He eventually needed to be carted off the floor. That wasn't the only big-time injury the Thunder suffered. In the first quarter, Cason Wallace sustained a torn labrum on his left shoulder. He tried to fight over Isaiah Jackson's screen. He will require surgery, too. Remains to be seen if it will end his 2026-27 season. Interesting to hear the Thunder say Williams will be checked on again before the 2027 NBA playoffs start. That leaves a window for him to make a miraculous return and help OKC in the postseason. Of course, we're a long ways away from that being within the realms of reality. item.title: Greise Kelly hails Brazil's composure in reaching U17 World Cup last eight
item.description: Greise Kelly hails Brazil's composure in reaching U17 World Cup last eight Named Player of the Match for the second time at the U-17 Women’s World Cup, Greise Kelly was once again one of the standout performers as Brazil advanced past Poland on Wednesday (28) in Morocco. Following a 3-3 draw in regulation time and a penalty shootout victory, the forward highlighted Brazil’s mental strength in overcoming the pressure and securing a place in the quarterfinals. For Greise, who captained the side in the match, the ability to handle adversity was key to Brazil’s comeback. “There was a lot of pressure in this match, both for us and for all the players. We knew it wouldn’t be easy because we had studied our opponents too. But it’s a killer—it really puts your heart through the wringer,” she said. Greise opens the scoring for Brazil against Poland in the World Cup round of 16 in Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Greise also highlighted the team’s composure, particularly amid the twists and turns of the second half. After falling behind, Brazil fought back, took the lead and remained competitive all the way through to the penalty shootout. “When you step onto the pitch, you have to be mentally present. I think Brazil show a very strong mentality because, when we went 2-1 down less than 15 minutes into the second half, we needed to control the chaos, and we did that very well. Personally, I managed that chaos really well. It’s no coincidence that I was named Player of the Match,” she reflected. Greise during the match against Poland in the U-17 World Cup round of 16 in Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF Player of the Match Her second Player of the Match award in four games marks another special moment for Greise in the tournament. Against Poland, the forward opened the scoring for Brazil. She was also heavily involved in other attacking moves and played a part in Marcelinha’s and Pepê’s goals during the match, which ended 3-3 in regulation time. Greise also converted her penalty in Brazil’s 8-7 shootout victory. The forward celebrated the recognition but made a point of sharing the credit with her Brazil teammates. “I’m so happy to receive this award for the second time. I think there’s a lot of hard work behind it. It’s not just about me; it’s always about them too,” she concluded. Brazil now await their quarterfinal opponents, who will be decided in Thursday’s (29) clash between China and France. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Ryan Day declines to name Ohio State football's starting quarterback for USC
item.description: Ohio State coach Ryan Day declined to name a starting quarterback following practice on Oct. 28. Day said freshman Luke Fahey and sophomore Tavien St. Clair have both practiced well as the Buckeyes prepare for this week’s game at USC without Julian Sayin behind center. “Both will be ready to play,” Day said. “Guys on the team have confidence that if both were put in the game, that they can do their job.” Day did little to tip his hand publicly about the pecking order at the position and sidestepped a question about whether he knew who would start against the Trojans . “Things have progressed this week similar to the way they have in the past,” Day said. “I’ll just leave it at that, keep preparing and play the game on Saturday.” Fahey has been seen as most likely to assume the starting role after he emerged as the No. 2 quarterback during preseason practices, surpassing St. Clair, who had arrived at Ohio State a year earlier as a decorated five-star prospect from Bellefontaine. Fahey replaced Sayin in the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes’ win at Indiana on Oct. 17 after he left with an injury . When Sayin was sacked by defensive lineman Mario Landino, the collision appeared to injure his right throwing arm, and he was later in a cast. He remains out indefinitely. But the Buckeyes began a midseason competition while they were idle last week, giving both Fahey and St. Clair first-team reps in practice. Nether has seen significant snaps for the Buckeyes. Fahey has completed nine of 13 passes for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions in four games. St. Clair has completed five of nine passes for 52 yards and one touchdown with one interception in three games since last season. Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. item.title: Big 12 instituting potential in-game penalties for discriminatory conduct at sporting events
item.description: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark gives his address during the league's football media days at The Star, the practice home of the Dallas Cowboys, in Frisco, Texas, on Tuesday, July 7, 2026. | Brandon Judd, Deseret News After the incident last Saturday in which some UCF fans in Orlando directed a derogatory chant at BYU and its sponsoring institution, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, the Big 12 Conference released a statement Wednesday that outlines some significant updates to penalties for violating its discriminatory conduct policy. Of particular note, the Big 12 announced that in-game penalties could occur for such violations, something many BYU fans and others have long been pining for. Here is the list of what the conference called “escalating consequences” for discriminatory actions displayed at its athletic events. A “confirmed” first incident will result in a $100,000 fine against the host institution. A formal warning will then follow, “providing the institution an opportunity to immediately address the behavior and prevent further incidents.” A second confirmed incident during the same game will result in in-game penalties such as a 15-yard unsportsmanlike penalty against the host team in football or an unsportsmanlike two-shot technical foul in basketball (examples of potential in-game penalties for other sports were not given). An additional $500,000 fine may also be levied against the host institution. Individuals ejected for discriminatory conduct will be “prohibited from attending all athletic events for the remainder of the academic year and are subject to applicable university fan/student conduct policies.” The Big 12 further noted that UCF did exhibit proper pregame policies on Saturday (in early October, the conference announced that 30-second commercials promoting sportsmanship would be played at every Big 12 sporting event) and immediate actions were taken against the offending chanters, but the institution will still be fined $100,000 by the conference. The introduction of in-game penalties by the conference is a major step as it tries to curb the increasingly frequent occurrences of opposing fans directing derogatory chants toward BYU and its sponsoring institution. Conference members Colorado and Oklahoma State had previously been fined for such incidents occurring at athletic events they hosted against BYU, but many felt those fines were not strong enough consequences for the actions. “The Big 12 remains committed to providing a respectful environment for student-athletes, coaches and fans,” the conference said in its statement. “Discriminatory conduct will not be tolerated, and the conference will continue working with its member institutions to prevent such behavior and ensure meaningful consequences when incidents occur.” The Big 12 logo is displayed on a pylon during the Big 12 championship game between BYU and Texas Tech held at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, on Saturday, Dec. 6, 2025. | Isaac Hale,

item.title: AI To Be Used in Shaping New Generation of F1 Cars As Part of FIA-AWS Deal
item.description: The FIA announced a new partnership with Amazon Web Services (AWS), but the key point that came up is the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to design new F1 cars. AWS has been a partner of F1 for some time; now it has inked a deal with the FIA as a global partner. It is now the ‘Official Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing, Machine Learning and Cloud Infrastructure’ partner of the governing body. It is also the ‘Official Partner of the FIA Awards and the FIA Sustainable Innovation Series’. As part of the deal, the governing body will use AWS’s technology to drive innovation and participation in motor racing. But the key part of the partnership is the use of AI to shape the new technical regulations for the next generation of F1 cars. Not just that, it will also help in the development of single-seater cars at large. What Does the FIA and AWS Deal Entails for F1 The FIA already runs its aerodynamic simulations on AWS’s High Performance Computing, which enables it to test the airflow around the car virtually, without the need for building physical parts. This not only makes things faster, but also saves costs and is an environmentally friendly option. The new deal will see the FIA provide AI tools to its technical and engineering teams to develop regulations keeping three points in mind – advanced safety, performance and sustainability. The current F1 regulations have largely come under fire not just from the drivers, but also from fans throughout. The complexity of the cars, with increased software use, is making things complicated when racing. The latest example was seen in Malaysia when a few cars stopped on track because the software did not understand why the F1 cars were driving slowly in damp conditions. The FIA was forced to quickly patch up an update, which delayed the start of the Grand Prix. Scrutiny Around Increased Software to Run F1 Cars The move to use AI in developing new F1 cars will certainly not sit well with the larger fan base, with the sport already under fire due to the 2026 regulations. A large portion of the blame has fallen on the V6 Hybrid Power Units for the dire state, but the increase in software to run the cars has not escaped scrutiny. Even in the US GP, Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson disclosed another software issue. Under the VSC, he was running in the delta time as set by the FIA. However, the system continued to beep in his ears, reminding him to slow down, even though he was running about six seconds below. F1 drivers have been vocal about the decreasing amount of driver input when racing, with software dictating much of the driving. This move could raise further questions about the priorities of the FIA in listening to the drivers to deliver a better product for racing, rather than making robots. item.title: WNBA Finals ticket for under $40? Game 6 matinee turns into a fire sale
item.description: A cluster of Golden State Valkyries fans in the stands before Game 4 of the WNBA Finals between Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries on Saturday at State Farm Arena. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) The WNBA Finals Game 6 time change from primetime to lunchtime is having a direct impact on ticket prices. The Atlanta Dream announced on Wednesday morning that State Farm Arena sold out its 17,000 capacity arena for the 12:30 p.m. ET tipoff on Thursday, but the get-in price to see the Golden State Valkyries' potential championship clincher - and the Dream's attempt to stop them - is substantially lower than the Game 4 matinee hosted on Saturday at State Farm Arena. Fans could get into Game 6 for $38 as of Wednesday morning, according to a spokesperson for TicketIQ.com . That's 85% lower than the get-in price for Game 4, which started at $246. The circumstances aren't ideal for fans who want to watch the WNBA's premier event. The game tips off midday on a weekday, while most are at work or at school. Further, anyone interested in watching the highest-stakes game yet had short notice to alter their Thursday plans. The WNBA and Dream didn't secure State Farm Arena until Monday morning, a few hours before Game 5, giving fans three days to buy their tickets. The league had to move tipoff from 8 p.m. to 12:30 p.m. ET to accommodate an Atlanta Hawks game on Thursday. That means the Valkyries could be hoisting the championship trophy while West Coast fans are enjoying brunch. The alternative would have been a primetime tipoff at Gateway Center Arena at College Park, the Dream's home court for a majority of the 2026 season that seats up to 3,500. The Dream are moving into State Farm Arena full time next season, but the arena is owned by the county and operated by the Hawks. The start of the NBA regular season overlaps with the WNBA Finals, forcing last-minute preparations to move Games 3, 4 and 6 into the bigger arena more suitable for the Finals stage. A potential Game 7 on Halloween Saturday evening at Chase Center has get-in prices listed at $359, according to TicketIQ.com . The time change should impact the broadcast partners' revenue, too. The game will be broadcast on USA Network, a basic cable channel, and streaming site Peacock. "The daytime window isn't perfect from a TV audience perspective," a USA Sports spokesperson said. "But the league had to make a really difficult decision taking a lot into account across multiple stakeholders. What was important to us was to ultimately be a good partner and to be part of the solution." Golden State's 67-62 win in Atlanta was the most-watched Game 4 in WNBA Finals history, according to NBC, with 1.9 million viewers on average (32% higher than last year) and 2.5 million at its peak. San Francisco led the market viewership with a 3.97 rating. An encore of Game 6 will air on Thursday at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on USA Network and CNBC - when the game originally would have been played. item.title: Torrent of takeaways has helped to spark Bucs’ turnaround
item.description: Bucs defensive tackle Calijah Kancey returns a fumble recovery 32 yards for a touchdown last Sunday against the Panthers in Charlotte, N.C. The fumble was forced by linebacker Al-Quadin Muhammad. ©Scott Kinser Every team preaches taking the football away, but the Bucs are repeating that sermon every Sunday. Tampa Bay has 12 takeaways this season, second most in the NFL only to the Packers. Eight of those turnovers have been forced in the past three games, a defensive effort that has led to a 2-1 resurgence after a 0-4 start. According to outside linebacker Yaya Diaby, the Bucs’ minister of defense has been A’Shawn Robinson, an interior defensive lineman who remarkably leads the team with two interceptions. “It’s just a mindset,” Diaby said. “It’s what we’ve been preaching the whole time. We’ve got a guy like A’Shawn who preaches it every day, man, and it’s starting to be contagious. So, really, we’ve got to keep doing what we’re doing, because it’s going good so far.” NFL teams that win the turnover battle win the game 79% of the time. From 1999 to 2025, teams with one extra takeaway in a game was worth about 4.5 points on the scoreboard, according to Vertize Sports . The Bucs rank third in the NFL in fewest total yards allowed per game (294.7) and second in rush defense (77.3 yards per game). Bucs linebacker Yaya Diaby celebrates one of his three sacks against the Panthers. The defense has recorded five sacks in each of the past two games. But to really be considered a great defense, you have to take the football away and hopefully score with it. That happened in the first half of the Bucs’ 43-13 win over the Panthers last Sunday. Outside linebacker Al-Quadin Muhammad sacked quarterback Bryce Young, forcing a fumble that was scooped up by defensive tackle Calijah Kancey, who raced 32 yards for a touchdown . “Man, you know that’s my dawg. item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns reacts after rushing for a touchdown in the first quarter against the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) Getty ATHENS, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 15: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns looks on during warmups before the game against the Georgia Bulldogs at Sanford Stadium on November 15, 2025 in Athens, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) Getty The Georgia Bulldogs have entered another conversation about Arch Manning’s future, this time through a prediction David Pollack attributed to an unnamed SEC coach. Pollack expressed confidence that Manning would leave Texas after the season. He then shared the coach’s belief that Georgia could become the quarterback’s next destination. For Bulldogs fans, the possibility creates an obvious reason to pay attention. A quarterback change involving Manning would attract national interest regardless of the destination. Connecting him to Athens adds a different dimension for supporters wondering what Georgia’s future offense could look like. However, the distinction between a prediction and a decision matters here. Pollack’s comments do not establish that Manning has chosen to transfer or that Georgia has secured his commitment. The destination claim comes through Pollack’s account of a private conversation. David Pollack Predicts Arch Manning Will Leave Texas “Arch will not be at Texas next year,” Pollack said. “This is something I heard from another SEC coach, and I believe 100% is going to happen.” Pollack’s confidence concerned Manning leaving Austin. His explanation suggested that he expects the quarterback to continue playing college football rather than immediately move to the professional level. That creates the opening for speculation about another program. “I think he is playing college, but not at Texas next year,” Pollack said. “It makes a lot of sense for both to go their own ways.” That remains Pollack’s assessment of the situation. It should not be confused with an announcement from Manning or Texas. Believing a separation would make sense does not establish that either side has decided to pursue one. Unnamed SEC Coach Connects Manning to Georgia Pollack then introduced the detail most relevant to Bulldogs supporters. According to his account, the same coach identified Georgia as a potential destination. Pollack declined to identify that coach. “That same coach that told me that actually said, ‘I think he will go to Georgia,’” Pollack said. The wording leaves room between expectation and certainty. An unnamed coach predicting Georgia does not establish contact with Kirby Smart, an offer or an agreement. None of those developments can be inferred from the quote alone. This early in the week, veteran players can be given time off, and that is no different for Chase. Chase missed five games in 2022 due to a hip injury. Chase produced 1,455 yards as a rookie, making the second-team All-Pro and being named the Offensive Rookie of the Year. In his second season, he played in 12 games and produced 1,046 yards. item.title: No penalty practice? No problem for Man City in shoot-out win
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca hugs goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli (PETER POWELL) Enzo Maresca admitted Manchester City did not practice penalties at all this season before beating Brighton & Hove Albion in a League Cup fourth round shoot-out on Wednesday. City goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli made two penalty saves as the League Cup holders won 4-3 in the shoot-out after twice coming from behind in a 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium. Maresca had opted against asking his players to practice penalties in training since his close-season arrival to replace Pep Guardiola. City's lack of spot-kick preparation was no problem thanks to reserve keeper Rulli, who denied Brighton's Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight. Mateo Kovacic did miss from the spot but Phil Foden, Enzo Fernandez, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki were all successful. "To be honest, since I've been here we never practised penalties," said Maresca, whose side will host third tier Bradford City for a place in the semi-finals. "We're very happy with the five, even Mateo. It always happens, the one that scored during the 90 minutes, and then misses the penalty." Kovacic had cancelled out Malick Yalcouye's opener for Brighton before half-time. Georginio Rutter restored the Seagulls' lead after the restart, but Vitor Reis diverted in a Cherki free-kick to take the match to penalties. "I'm not sure he changed the game, but for sure he made an impact," said Maresca of Belgian winger Doku. "This is the reason why they are there – when they start from the beginning, to try to do their best, and if they go on from the bench, to try to make an impact." City had suffered their first Premier League defeat this season on Saturday, losing at Aston Villa to end their 100 percent start to the top-flight campaign. It was vital for City to bounce back with a win against Brighton as they try to remain positive while awaiting the verdict in their appeal against a guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules. If the appeal fails, City could be hit with a massive points deduction that would effectively lead to relegation. In the midst of a pressure-packed schedule, Maresca had no regrets about his decision to rest Erling Haaland, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Ruben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Josko Gvardiol against Brighton. "I was happy with the way we planned the game, with the rotation, and especially I was very, very, very happy with the ones that were playing," he said. Maresca, who made nine changes, praised Donnarumma's deputy Rulli for his composed display. "Apart from the penalties, I think overall he was good, especially in the build-up. He also made a good save," he said. smg/bsp
